title: The Young Inventor's Workshop
summary: A girl who loves building things in her garage workshop enters a school invention fair with a clever gadget, and must calmly troubleshoot it when it fails during the first test.
poll: If your invention fails in front of judges, it is better to give up than try to fix it on the spot.

versions.title: The Young Inventor's Workshop
versions.text:
Maya loves to build things. She has a small workshop. It is in the garage. She uses her dad's old tools.

The school has an invention fair. Maya wants to invent something new. She picks a plant waterer. It drips water on its own.

Maya builds her gadget. It has a tube and a timer. She tests it at home. It works just right!

On fair day, Maya sets up her table. Judges come to see it. Maya turns it on.

Oh no! It does not drip. It floods the plant! Water goes on the table.

Maya does not give up. She stays calm. She looks at the tube. The hole is too big.

Maya fixes the tube. She makes the hole small. She tests it again. It drips just right!

The judges smile. Maya is proud. She built it, and she fixed it too.

versions.title: The Young Inventor's Workshop
versions.text:
Maya loves to build things more than anything else in the world. She has her own small workshop in the garage. She uses her dad's old tools there nearly every weekend.

One week, the school has an invention fair. Maya decides right away to invent something new. She picks an automatic plant waterer: a gadget that drips water into a plant on its own.

Maya builds her gadget with just a tube and a simple timer. She tests it at home first, and it works just right. It drips a little water slowly into the soil.

On the morning of the fair, Maya sets up her table and waits. A group of judges walks over to see her gadget up close. Maya turns it on so they can watch it work.

Oh no! This time the gadget refuses to drip at all. It suddenly floods the little plant with too much water! Water quickly spills across the whole table.

Maya does not give up or panic in front of everyone watching. She forces herself to stay calm and looks closely at the tube. She sees that the hole is far too big.

Maya fixes the tube herself, making the hole much smaller than it was. She tests the gadget once more, and this time it drips the water just right.

The judges smile and nod with real approval. Maya feels very proud of herself. She built a clever gadget, and she fixed it on her own.

versions.title: The Young Inventor's Workshop
versions.text:
Maya has loved building things for a long time. Her workshop in the garage is full of her father's old tools. It is her favorite place in the house. She spends nearly every weekend there, inventing something new.

One week, the school announces an invention fair. Maya decides to design an automatic plant waterer. It is a gadget that drips water into a plant's soil, so no one has to remember to do it.

She assembles her gadget from a thin tube and a simple timer. At home, it works well. It gives a slow, steady drip of water at just the right time.

On the morning of the fair, Maya sets up her table. A panel of judges comes to see each invention. She turns her gadget on, eager to show how it works.

Instead of a gentle drip, the gadget seems to malfunction. It floods the plant with a rush of water, spilling across the table in front of everyone!

Rather than panicking, Maya stays calm. She inspects the tube closely and notices that the opening is far wider than it should be.

She fixes the problem on the spot, making the opening narrower with a steady hand. She tests the gadget once more, and this time it drips the water just right.

The judges nod with real approval. They are impressed by her quick thinking and by the gadget itself. Maya feels proud for building something clever, and for solving the problem herself.

versions.title: The Young Inventor's Workshop: Fixing the Gadget
versions.text:
Maya had loved building things for as long as she could remember, and her small workshop in the garage, filled with her father's old, well-worn tools, was easily her favorite place in the entire house. She spent nearly every weekend out there, inventing something new instead of watching television with her friends.

One week, the school announced an invention fair open to every student in her grade, complete with real judges and a small prize for the most impressive design. Maya decided almost immediately to design an automatic plant waterer, a device that would drip water into a plant's soil without anyone having to remember to do it themselves.

She meticulously assembled her gadget from a thin plastic tube and a simple timer she had found in a kitchen drawer. At home, it functioned perfectly, releasing a slow, steady drip of water exactly when it should, hour after hour, day after day.

On the morning of the fair, Maya set up her table and waited nervously as a panel of judges slowly approached to examine each student's invention one after another. She switched her gadget on, eager to demonstrate precisely how it worked in front of them.

Instead of a gentle drip, the gadget suddenly malfunctioned, flooding the little plant with a rush of water that spilled across the table in front of everyone watching closely and curiously.

Rather than panicking in front of the judges, Maya forced herself to remain composed and inspected the tube closely, piece by piece, the way a real engineer might diagnose a malfunction. She quickly discovered that the opening in the tube was far wider than it ought to have been.

She resolved the problem right there on the spot, narrowing the opening meticulously with a steady hand, then tested the gadget once more in front of everyone. This time, it dripped the water exactly right, slow and steady, just as it had at home.

The judges nodded with genuine admiration, clearly impressed as much by her quick thinking under pressure as by the gadget itself. Maya felt immensely proud, not merely for building something clever, but for diagnosing and solving the problem entirely on her own.

versions.title: The Young Inventor's Workshop: Fixing the Gadget
versions.text:
Maya had loved building things for as long as she could remember, and her small workshop in the garage, filled with her father's old, well-worn tools, was easily her favorite place in the entire house, considerably more inviting than any other room she could possibly name. She spent nearly every weekend out there, inventing something new instead of watching television with her friends down the street.

One week, the school announced an invention fair open to every student in her grade, complete with real judges and a small prize awarded for the most impressive design submitted that particular year. Maya decided almost immediately to design an automatic plant waterer, a device that would drip water into a plant's soil without anyone having to remember to do it themselves each day.

She meticulously assembled her gadget from a thin plastic tube and a simple timer she had found in a kitchen drawer, testing each connection carefully beforehand. At home, it functioned perfectly, releasing a slow, steady drip of water exactly when it should, hour after hour, day after day, without any trouble at all.

On the morning of the fair, Maya set up her table and waited nervously as a panel of judges slowly approached to examine each student's invention one after another, taking careful notes as they went about their methodical inspection. She switched her gadget on, eager to demonstrate precisely how it worked.

Instead of a gentle drip, the gadget suddenly malfunctioned, flooding the little plant with a rush of water that spilled across the table in front of everyone watching closely and curiously, murmuring amongst themselves.

Rather than panicking in front of the judges, Maya forced herself to remain composed and inspected the tube closely, piece by piece, the way a real engineer might methodically diagnose a malfunction under considerable pressure. She quickly discovered that the opening in the tube was considerably wider than it ought to have been.

She resolved the problem right there on the spot, narrowing the opening meticulously with a steady hand while the judges watched intently, then tested the gadget once more in front of everyone. This time, it dripped the water exactly right, slow and steady, just as it had at home earlier that week.

The judges nodded with genuine admiration, clearly impressed as much by her quick thinking under pressure as by the ingenuity of the gadget itself. Maya felt immensely proud, not merely for building something clever, but for diagnosing and solving the problem entirely on her own, without any help at all from anyone nearby.

versions.title: The Young Inventor's Workshop: Fixing the Gadget
versions.text:
Maya had cultivated a passion for building things for as long as she could remember, and her modest workshop in the garage, populated with her father's old, well-worn tools, was unquestionably her favorite place in the entire house, considerably more inviting than any other room she could possibly name. She spent nearly every weekend out there, inventing something new instead of watching television with her friends down the street, who often teased her affectionately about her unconventional hobby.

One week, the school administration announced an invention fair open to every student in her grade, complete with genuine, qualified judges and a small prize awarded for the most impressive design submitted that particular academic year. Maya decided almost immediately to design an automatic plant waterer, a device that would dispense water into a plant's soil without anyone having to remember to perform the task themselves each day.

She meticulously assembled her gadget from a thin plastic tube and a simple timer she had discovered in a kitchen drawer, methodically testing every connection beforehand to avoid any unforeseen complications later. At home, it functioned flawlessly, releasing a slow, steady drip of water exactly when it should, hour after hour, day after day, without any trouble whatsoever.

On the morning of the fair, Maya set up her table and waited nervously as a panel of distinguished judges slowly approached to examine each student's invention one after another, taking careful notes as they proceeded methodically through the crowded rows of tables. She switched her gadget on, eager to demonstrate precisely how it functioned.

Instead of a gentle drip, the gadget suddenly malfunctioned unexpectedly, flooding the little plant with an uncontrolled rush of water that spilled across the table in front of everyone watching closely and curiously, several of them murmuring in evident surprise.

Rather than succumbing to panic in front of the judges, Maya forced herself to remain composed and inspected the tube closely, piece by piece, the way a seasoned engineer might methodically diagnose a malfunction under genuine pressure. She quickly discovered that the opening in the tube was considerably wider than it ought reasonably to have been.

She resolved the problem right there on the spot, meticulously narrowing the opening with a steady hand while the judges watched intently from just a few feet away, then tested the gadget once more in front of everyone present. This time, it dripped the water exactly right, slow and steady, precisely as it had at home earlier that week.

The judges nodded with genuine admiration, clearly impressed as much by her quick thinking under considerable pressure as by the underlying ingenuity of the gadget itself. Maya felt immensely proud, not merely for constructing something clever, but for diagnosing and resolving the problem entirely independently, without any assistance whatsoever from anyone standing nearby.

keyWords.definition: to design and build something new that did not exist before
keyWords.example: She likes to invent small toys out of cardboard.

keyWords.definition: a small, clever machine or tool made to do a job
keyWords.example: My uncle has a gadget that opens jars easily.

keyWords.definition: a long, hollow pipe that liquid or air can move through
keyWords.example: Water flowed down the tube into the bucket.

keyWords.definition: to cover something with too much water
keyWords.example: Heavy rain can flood a low street quickly.

keyWords.definition: to repair something so it works correctly
keyWords.example: Dad can fix the broken chair with some glue.

questions.stem: What is this story mostly about?
options: A girl who buys a new plant for her room
A school that builds a new garden for students
A girl who builds a gadget and fixes it when it fails
A girl who loses her favorite tool in the garage at home
questions.why: The story follows Maya as she builds a gadget, watches it fail, and then fixes it at the fair.

wrong.A: The story is about building a gadget, not buying a plant.
wrong.B: The invention fair is about gadgets, not a garden.
wrong.D: Maya does not lose a tool in the story.

questions.stem: What gadget does Maya decide to build for the fair?
options: a robot that walks
a toy car that races
an automatic plant waterer
a light for reading books
questions.why: The story says Maya decides to build an automatic plant waterer that drips water into a plant.

wrong.A: The story does not mention a walking robot.
wrong.B: The story does not mention a racing toy car.
wrong.D: The story does not mention a reading light.

questions.stem: What happens when Maya first turns on her gadget at the fair?
options: It does not turn on
It drips water perfectly, just like at home
It makes a loud beeping sound
It floods the plant with too much water
questions.why: The story says that instead of dripping, the gadget floods the plant and water spills onto the table.

wrong.A: The gadget does turn on; it just does not work correctly.
wrong.B: It works at home, but not at the fair.
wrong.C: The story does not mention any beeping sound.

questions.stem: In the story, to fix something means to —
options: build something brand new
repair it so it works right
throw it away completely
make it louder than before
questions.why: Maya fixes the tube by repairing the hole so the gadget works correctly again.

wrong.A: Fixing is repairing, not building something new.
wrong.C: Maya repairs the gadget; she does not throw it away.
wrong.D: Fixing the tube is not about making noise.

questions.stem: Why does Maya stay calm instead of panicking when her gadget floods the plant?
options: She wants to think clearly and solve the problem
She does not care about the invention fair or her project
She plans to leave the fair right away
She does not notice the water
questions.why: Maya stays calm so she can look closely at the problem and figure out how to fix it.

wrong.B: Maya cares enough to fix the gadget right there.
wrong.C: Maya stays at the fair and fixes her gadget.
wrong.D: Maya clearly notices the flood of water.

questions.stem: Why does the gadget flood the plant instead of dripping water slowly?
options: The timer is set for the wrong time
The hole in the tube is too big
The tube is blocked
The plant does not need any water
questions.why: Maya finds that the hole in the tube is too wide, which lets too much water through at once.

wrong.A: The story does not say the timer is wrong.
wrong.C: A blocked tube would stop water, not flood it.
wrong.D: The plant does need water; that is the point of the gadget.

questions.stem: What does Maya do right after she notices the hole in the tube is too big?
options: She asks the judges for a new gadget
She waters the plant by hand instead
She makes the hole smaller
She throws the gadget away
questions.why: After finding the problem, Maya fixes the tube by making the hole smaller before testing it again.

wrong.A: The story does not mention asking for a new gadget.
wrong.B: Maya fixes the gadget instead of watering by hand.
wrong.D: Maya fixes the gadget rather than throwing it away.

questions.stem: How is Maya's gadget different at the end of the story compared to when it first failed?
options: It is exactly the same and still floods the plant
It drips the water just right after she fixes it
It no longer turns on
It waters a different plant instead
questions.why: After fixing the hole in the tube, the gadget finally drips water correctly, unlike its first failed test.

wrong.A: The gadget works correctly after Maya's fix.
wrong.C: The gadget turns on and works at the end.
wrong.D: The gadget waters the same plant throughout the story.

LOW.prompt: Imagine your invention failed in front of judges, like Maya's did. Write about how you would stay calm and try to fix the problem.
checklist: I explained how I would stay calm.
I explained how I would try to fix the problem.
I wrote complete sentences with capital letters and periods.
LOW.modelAnswer: If my invention failed like Maya's did, I would try to stay calm instead of panicking. I would look closely at my gadget to find the exact problem, just like Maya looked at the tube. Then I would try to fix that one part instead of giving up. Staying calm would help me think clearly and fix my gadget.

keyWords.definition: to put the parts of something together to build it
keyWords.example: It took an hour to assemble the new bookshelf.

keyWords.definition: to fail to work the way it is supposed to
keyWords.example: The elevator began to malfunction and stopped between floors.

keyWords.definition: to look at something closely and carefully
keyWords.example: The mechanic inspected the car's engine for problems.

keyWords.definition: firm, calm, and not shaking or changing suddenly
keyWords.example: She kept a steady hand while painting the small details.

keyWords.definition: feeling admiration because something was done well
keyWords.example: The coach was impressed by how fast the team improved.

questions.stem: Which sentence best tells what this story is mainly about?
options: A girl's gadget fails at a fair, and she calmly finds and fixes the problem
A girl decides never to build gadgets again after one small failure in front of the judges
A school fair is cancelled because too many gadgets break down
A girl wins a prize for the fastest robot built that year
questions.why: The story follows Maya through her gadget's failure and her calm, successful repair at the fair.

wrong.B: Maya keeps building and even fixes the gadget that day.
wrong.C: The fair is not cancelled in the story.
wrong.D: The story focuses on a plant waterer, not a racing robot.

options: a small motor and a battery
a thin tube and a simple timer
a fan and a light bulb
a sensor and a tiny screen
questions.why: In the story, Maya assembles her gadget from a thin tube and a simple timer.

wrong.A: The story does not mention a motor or battery.
wrong.C: The story does not mention a fan or light bulb.
wrong.D: The story does not mention a sensor or screen.

options: a battery and a small fan
a box and a little bell
a thin tube and a timer
a cup and a metal spoon
questions.why: In the story, Maya builds her gadget from a thin tube and a simple timer.

wrong.A: A fan is not part of her gadget.
wrong.B: A bell is not part of it.
wrong.D: A cup and spoon are not named.

questions.stem: In the story, the word malfunction most nearly means —
options: to work exactly as planned
to become louder than usual
to look more attractive
to fail to work correctly
questions.why: The gadget malfunctions when it suddenly floods the plant instead of working as it should.

wrong.A: Malfunctioning is the opposite of working as planned.
wrong.B: Malfunctioning is not about becoming louder.
wrong.C: Malfunctioning is not about appearance.

questions.stem: Why does Maya inspect the tube piece by piece instead of guessing what went wrong?
options: She wants to find the exact cause of the problem
She is simply bored while waiting for judges
She forgot how she built the gadget

MID.prompt: Explain how Maya used calm, careful thinking to turn her gadget's failure at the fair into a success. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained how Maya stayed calm.
I explained how she found and fixed the problem.
I used at least two details from the story.
MID.modelAnswer: When Maya's gadget suddenly malfunctioned and flooded the plant in front of the judges, she did not panic. Instead, she stayed calm and inspected the tube piece by piece to find the exact cause of the problem. She discovered that the opening in the tube was too wide, so she narrowed it with a steady hand. Because she tested the gadget again right away, she was able to show the judges a working invention, and they nodded with real approval at both her gadget and her quick thinking.

HIGH.prompt: The story suggests that how an inventor responds to failure matters as much as the invention itself. Do you agree or disagree? Support your answer with evidence from Maya's experience.
checklist: I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed a point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that how an inventor responds to failure matters as much as the invention itself. Maya's gadget malfunctioned in the worst possible moment, right in front of the judges, yet what truly impressed them was not a perfect first test but her composed, meticulous diagnosis of the problem. By inspecting the tube piece by piece and narrowing the opening with a steady hand, she showed the kind of thinking a real engineer relies on. Someone might argue that the invention itself, the clever idea of an automatic waterer, deserves most of the credit, and that is a fair point, but without Maya's calm response to its failure, the judges would have seen only a broken gadget rather than a resourceful inventor.
